problem: VLM-based ObjectNav policies either use first-person RGB with low-level action prediction (short-horizon, repetitive: turning in place, backtracking) or text summaries of maps that lose spatial structure and visual detail. Existing learned policies are also trained on oracle shortest-path data rather than human search under partial observability.
motivation: Humans search efficiently by combining spatial memory (where they have been, what is unexplored) with visual cues about promising areas. Human demonstrations contain this search intent but only as low-level actions, so a way to recover waypoint-level intent and a representation that keeps spatial and visual evidence aligned are needed for long-horizon search.
key_idea: Recover candidate-level (frontier/target) waypoint labels from low-level human demonstrations by looking ahead at frontier evolution, and train a VLM to select among BEV-grounded candidates, each paired with its first-observed egocentric image and agent-relative geometry, using an angular soft-target objective.
insight: The gains come from the candidate-level BEV interface and grounding: random BEV candidate selection (58.7 SR) already beats the egocentric action policy (35.4), and a reserved candidate-ID output beats text coordinates (82.2 vs 68.4 SR on HM3D-v2). Removing visual memory causes the largest drop (70.2 SR), oracle semantics push to 84.6, and frontier-collapse labels beat heading or trajectory matching (53.8 vs 38.9/42.0 SR on MP3D). Angular soft targets help only if applied to frontier steps, not target steps (soft everywhere 77.8 SR vs 82.2).
method: Candidate-level formulation: from RGB-D, maintain a persistent BEV map (occupancy, explored, agent footprint, trajectory) and build a candidate set of frontier and verified target waypoints (max 32); the VLM picks one index, which a local planner executes, decoupling it from the embodiment.

Frontier-based Human-Intent Labeling: replay Habitat-Web demonstrations, advance at least 6 forward moves, find the first future step t+ where a current frontier drifts beyond a threshold from the future frontier set, and label the candidate with the largest geodesic distance to F_{t+} (i.e. the one the human explored through); a target candidate is used directly when present.

Candidate visual memory and agent-centric geometry: each candidate carries the egocentric RGB from when it was first created plus [normalized distance, sin, cos of relative bearing], injected via a pairwise spatial encoder into the <cand> token embeddings.

Candidate-aligned VLM input: a BEV crop plus serialized candidate blocks are processed by separate BEV and ego ViTs (InternViT, independent LoRA); the output is one of 32 reserved <id_k> tokens with a restricted softmax.
Intent-Aligned Objective: a von Mises-style angular soft target (sigma=25°) over candidates is blended with hard CE (lambda=0.3) on frontier steps; target steps use hard CE only (target-safe).

Target proposal and verification: detections must be positive in 2 of the last 3 frames, are back-projected to 3D, snapped to a navigable point, and removed if missed repeatedly; simulator semantics are used in training replay, and an open-vocabulary detector or YOLOE at test time.

setting.backbone: InternVL3-2B (InternViT-300M + Qwen2-1.5B), fine-tuned with LoRA plus new spatial modules and dual ViT
setting.training_data: Habitat-Web human ObjectNav demos replayed on 28 MP3D train scenes, 21 categories, 23,767 episodes, giving 2,363,108 candidate-level samples; no HM3D training
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, 79° FoV) with pose, building a BEV map; LiDAR+SLAM+RGB in real world
setting.action_space: discrete candidate waypoints (frontier or target) chosen from up to 32 BEV candidates, executed by a shortest-path follower or local planner
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D, HM3D-v1, HM3D-v2) plus real world
setting.privileged: none at test time (agent pose from simulator; simulator semantics only for training-label construction)

numbers_note: HM3D-v1 and HM3D-v2 both map to HM3D-ObjNav; the paper says 'validation benchmarks' without naming the split beyond MP3D-Val, so 'val' is used. Real-world results are qualitative only (no success rates given).
results: IntentNav gets SR/SPL of 53.8/23.1 on MP3D, 70.5/34.6 on HM3D-v1 and 82.2/38.5 on HM3D-v2, the best SR on all three and above every learning-based baseline. It also beats the training-free STRIVE and SysNav on SR (e.g. 82.2 vs 80.8 on HM3D-v2), while SPL is tied or slightly below STRIVE on HM3D-v2 (38.5 vs 38.7). The same checkpoint is deployed on wheeled, quadruped and humanoid robots.
limitations: Assumes a mostly static environment; stale BEV regions and visual memories in dynamic scenes hurt frontier extraction and ranking.
High-level selection is decoupled from local planning, so execution failures and detours are not fed back to the VLM.

Relies on a good external detector and target-verification pipeline. Real-world evaluation is qualitative (8 categories, 10 scenes) with no reported success rates, and VLM latency is 1.3 s per decision, growing with candidate count.
